minutes.headline: Task force will draft a non-binding article asking town meeting to choose stormwater utility vs. operating budget funding
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force reviewed impervious-surface billing data reconciled against the assessor's roll, settled on an ERU-based flat-fee approach rather than tiers, and discussed an abatement/credit program for commercial properties. Most of the meeting planned the path to the November 17 special town meeting: a non-binding straw poll on utility vs. operating-budget funding, a warrant article due September 17, a schedule of FinCom, Select Board and public information sessions in October/November, and a two-meeting process (around September 8 and 14) to draft, share and vote on the article language before sending it to town counsel Adam.

budget_items.what_was_said: After reconciling impervious-surface data with the assessor's roll, the consultant said the final flat per-household number came out around this figure and the task force preferred a flat fee over calculating perable area per residence.
The task force said there were questions on four properties and that they had gotten answers, citing this figure in the discussion of one parcel.
Two properties approaching a million square feet were cited as an example of how high a utility fee could get for very large non-residential parcels.
A comparison town's abatement system was described as capping relief at this level, described as a powerful incentive for commercial property owners to improve stormwater management.

The finance committee's objection to the utility approach centered on overhead described as around this share of the budget; a member argued the same share of overhead would exist under an operating-budget approach too.

budget_items.topic: Override amount for stormwater engineer position
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force recalled the failed override figure proposed to fund a junior engineer position, unsure whether it would need to change for the next attempt.
Because the junior engineer position would also do other DPW project-manager work, the task force suggested only about half the position's cost should be attributed to the stormwater comparison.

decisions.decision: Task force agreed to bill using an ERU (equivalent residential unit) approach based on actual impervious surface area rather than a tiered fee structure.
Agreed the warrant article should include enough financial/rate substance for voters to understand the choice, but should not include a draft bylaw.
Agreed stormwater fees will be billed separately from the property tax bill, with an option for residents to pay quarterly via a tear-off coupon.
Agreed municipal parcels will not be billed, but nonprofits and churches will be billed like any other property.
Agreed the task force needs to vote on the article language itself before it can be submitted, and that members cannot deliberate over email/BCC due to open meeting rules.
Set a schedule of two meetings (around September 8 and September 14) to draft, review, and vote on the article before sending it to town counsel Adam ahead of the September 17 warrant deadline.

Planned FinCom presentation for October 8, Select Board presentation for October 20, and a public information session in the first week of November (around November 3), spaced roughly two weeks apart ahead of the November 17 town meeting.

what_happened.line: The task force will ask a non-binding straw poll of town meeting to choose between a stormwater utility fee and continuing to fund stormwater work through the operating budget.
Members settled on billing every property a flat fee based on its impervious surface (an ERU approach) rather than tiered rates, if a utility is chosen.
Fees would be billed separately from the property tax bill, payable quarterly by tear-off coupon; municipal land would not be billed but churches and nonprofits would be.
A warrant article is due September 17, with two task force meetings around September 8 and 14 to draft and vote on its language before sending it to town counsel.
FinCom hears the proposal October 8, the Select Board October 20, and a public information session is planned around November 3, ahead of the November 17 special town meeting.

why_it_matters: Depending on which funding path town meeting favors in the non-binding vote, residents could see stormwater costs shift from the tax bill to a new separate utility bill tied to a property's paved and roofed area.
Churches, nonprofits and large commercial parcels would be billed under a utility approach even though they are often exempt from property tax, while town-owned land would not be billed.
The vote at town meeting is advisory only; the operating-budget alternative includes a stormwater engineer position that failed as an override once already.
